Type, priority (Urgent from 'Give urgent attention') and and/or structure are faithful, including nested anaphylaxis, glucose/diabetes and pregnancy clauses. Problems: asymmetry dropped (over-triggers on any sudden weakness), vaccination not tied to the collapse or recency, allergen timing dropped. Applying the red box to 'Falls' as well as collapse goes beyond the box header ('patient who has collapsed'), a minor stretch.

summary: Most consequential: the orthostatic test encodes only 'systolic drop ≥ 20' and drops 'or diastolic drop ≥ 10', so the orthostatic hypotension rule misses diastolic-only cases and the hyperventilation/common-faint rules wrongly fire for them. The red-box stroke/TIA criteria lose 'asymmetric' and the allergen/vaccination criteria lose their timing, which broadens Urgent triage. Rules also omit page content such as 'anaemia likely' (Hb < 12/13) and same-day referral for abnormal ECG; glucose should use 'Blood glucose concentration'.
